bull.b: Formal long-term supplier agreements with Astronics (power systems) and Hyundai WIA (landing gear) materially de‑risk key aircraft subsystems. Secured, aerospace‑grade suppliers improve manufacturability, certification readiness and increase likelihood of scaled production once type design is frozen.

The move from demonstration toward certification — expanded Permit to Fly, two‑way piloted transitions, added prototype, and a rebaselined CDR/2029 target — shows the program is advancing through regulatory milestones. This structural shift strengthens the path to revenue generation once type certification and production readiness are achieved.

Access to up to $850M of financing and a reported ~$96M cash balance provide tangible runway to fund certification, testing and early production activities. This funding buffer reduces immediate solvency risk and supports multi‑year engineering and industrialisation investment required before commercial revenues commence.

bear.b: With virtually no recognized revenue over multiple years and continued heavy operating losses, the company remains pre‑commercial. Long‑term value depends entirely on achieving certification and converting preorders; delays or demand shortfalls would leave the business without a sustainable revenue stream and reliant on external funding.

Negative equity across recent years and debt materially exceeding assets by 2025 constrain financial flexibility. Elevated leverage raises refinancing and covenant risks, reduces ability to absorb certification cost overruns, and can impair negotiating leverage with suppliers and customers during industrialisation phases.

Consistent negative operating and free cash flows indicate weak cash generation; the 2025 FCF burn (~-$78M) and operating cash deficits force ongoing reliance on financing. Reported net income improvements are not matched by operating cash, highlighting low earnings quality and sustained dilution or refinancing risk until commercial operations produce positive cash flows.
